name: project_behavior_listing_column
description: "Behaviors leave the read-time aggregation for watchers.last_run_completed_at — the conversations-row approach was BUILT then REJECTED as over-engineered; branch feat/behavior-listing-rows needs a full rewrite (2 unpushed commits to reset)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:10:31.116Z
---

Prerequisite for [[project_recent_feed_unified]]. Worktree
`.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows`, branch `feat/behavior-listing-rows`,
PORT 9186. **Two commits exist (34f1d50f4, 7953833cb) and are UNPUSHED — reset
them; the approach they implement was rejected.**

## The bug

`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
grows with run history forever.

Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
4 active / 56 archived org-wide).

## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)

Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.

## ACCEPTED approach

One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.

- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
  is ~60 rows in prod)
- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.

**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.

## Keep from the rejected branch

The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
assertion holds under either design; proved red against
`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.

## Gotchas hit

- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated

- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.

Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
shipping the backfill**.

---
name: reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution
description: "How an MCP client is identified (6 signals on oauth_clients + events.client_id), the display-name precedence conflict between two surfaces, and the fact that conversations carries NO client attribution — measured on prod 2026-07-30"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
---

## ChatGPT DOES create conversations — I was wrong twice

Measured on prod 2026-07-30. Do not repeat the claim that MCP clients only call
read tools; it is false.

```
ChatGPT | run_sdk 498 · query_sql 123 · query_sdk 32 · search_sdk 28 · search_memory 6 · save_memory 2
Claude  | run_sdk 1244 · query_sql 1224 · …
```

Of ChatGPT's `run_sdk` calls, **13 are `conversations.send`** — real agent
conversations. One is live in the listing right now:
`personal-agent_8a2D2Yb…_8dc12bdd…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5`, surfaced as
`{"id":"mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5","platform":"web"}`. ChatGPT's dominant SDK path
is `operations.execute` (539) — it drives the Chrome extension.

Method that works: `events` JOIN `oauth_clients` on `e.client_id`, then
`jsonb_array_elements(payload_data->'sdk_call_trace')` for `path` and `args`.
`conversations` itself is NOT in the MCP query allowlist.

## The six identity signals

Five on `oauth_clients`, one per-invocation:

| signal | when written | ChatGPT's value |
|---|---|---|
| `client_name` | DCR registration | `ChatGPT` |
| `metadata.last_client_info.name/title` | MCP `initialize`, per session | `openai-mcp` |
| `metadata.last_user_agent` | HTTP header | `openai-mcp/1.0.0` |
| `software_id` / `software_version` | DCR software statement | null |
| `redirect_uris` host | OAuth callback | `chatgpt.com` |
| `events.client_id` | every tool call | the only PER-INVOCATION signal |

Also `metadata.last_capabilities` — ChatGPT alone declares `openai/visibility`
and `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. `recordMcpClientActivity`
(`mcp-handler.ts:619` → `touchClientActivity`) writes the first three on every
authenticated request.

## Two surfaces disagree on the name

`client-routes.ts:258` uses `clientInfo.name || client_name` — clientInfo WINS.
`client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite.
**5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered as**, because
clientInfo reflects the process driving the connection, not the app:

```
Owletto for Mac → claude-code   (×3)
Lobu CLI        → claude-code
Claude          → claude-code
```

Trustworthy identity = `redirect_uris` host + `software_id` (can't be
self-reported away). `clientInfo` answers "what is driving it" — a different
question worth its own field, not an override.

## The attribution gap

`events.client_id` knows. **`conversations` does not** — the write path stores
`kind='owned'` → `platform:'web'` and drops the client. So ChatGPT, Claude, the
CLI and the browser all land in one undifferentiated bucket, and no query can
separate them. This is why there is no ChatGPT icon in Recent, and it is the same
missing field as the shared-thread attribution gap. Fix = `conversations.client_id`
written where the run is minted.

## last_seen_at exists; agent scoping does not

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is live on all 19 prod rows (Claude 17:43,
ChatGPT 17:10 on 2026-07-30) — the MCP equivalent of
`watchers.last_run_completed_at` already exists, no migration needed.

But `metadata.last_agent_id` is **NULL on all 19 rows** — `touchClientActivity`
only sets it `if (params.agentId)` and `authCtx.agentId` is evidently unset on
these requests. `client-routes.ts:255` filters
`if (agentId && assignedAgentId !== agentId) return null`, so that agent filter
currently drops every client. Per-agent MCP client rows need that write fixed
first; root cause not yet traced.

Related: [[project_recent_feed_unified]],
[[project_mcp_clients_as_external_agents]],
[[reference_behavior_conversation_id_is_client_forgeable]].

---
name: reference_conversation_id_is_a_session_key
description: "Why conversations has both conversation_id and thread_id — the web conversation_id is really a BullMQ/session/SSE key, so thread_id exists to pull a routable identity back out of it; conversation branching (parent_*) is designed but unbuilt"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
---

## The two ids

```
conversation_id: REDACTED…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5
thread_id:       mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5
```

|              | owned / web                        | platform                  |
|--------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| id shape     | `{agent}_{user}_{org}_{suffix}`    | `slack:D095U1QV667`       |
| separator    | `_` (BullMQ job ids ban `:`)       | `:`                       |
| `thread_id`  | the suffix                         | **null**                  |
| routes as    | `/chat/c/{threadId}`               | `/conversations/{conversationId}` |

`thread_id` was added by `20260727150000_conversations_thread_id.sql` to stop
reconstructing the route segment from `conversation_id` on every list read —
the same materialize-don't-derive instinct as
[[project_behavior_listing_column]].

## Why the web id is packed

`agent.ts:~898`: `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` is a GLOBAL constant, so without userId +
org baked in, two tenants could collide on one conversation id and resume each
other's session. The same string is simultaneously the BullMQ job id, the
session-store key, and the SSE owner-routing key.

**That is the debt: conversation identity is welded to the machine session key.**
`thread_id` is the patch that pulls a user-facing identity back out. Identical
conflation to `{agentId}_watcher_<id>_run_<runId>`, where run identity was welded
to listing identity. If a conversation had its own opaque primary identity and
the session key merely referenced it, `thread_id` would not exist, both routing
rules would collapse into one, and branching would have something stable to point
at. NOT worth refactoring now — that packed id is parsed by the MCP
unattended-tool gate, drives worker dispatch + SSE routing, and is guarded by the
sdk-e2e gate. Branching will force the issue.

## thread_id gates listability

The `conversations_fill_thread_id` trigger only fills when the id matches the
exact `{agent}_{user}_{org}_` prefix; otherwise NULL. `agent-thread-list.ts:221`
skips any owned row without one. **So an MCP client that invents its own
`conversationId` in a non-packed shape gets a working conversation that never
appears in Recent** — consistent with `e2e-conversation-ms28twyo` (bare custom
id) being absent from the prod listing while `mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5` (packed) is
present.

## Nesting

Platform ids already encode `{platform}:{channel}:{thread}` — `isConversationVisible`
splits on `:` and takes `parts[1]` as the channel for the ACL. So container→leaf
nesting exists, but only as string structure.

Modelled lineage does NOT exist. The original migration deferred it explicitly —
"branch lineage (`parent_*`) columns are introduced by the follow-ups that
actually read/write them" — and no conversations migration since adds it
(`sandbox_pin`, `thread_id`, `is_direct` only). Matches
[[project_home_chat_conversation_branching_arch]] (fork unbuilt).

## kind vs platform

`kind` is 100% derivable from `platform` today — `classifyConversation` is the
sole writer: `platform === 'api'` → `{kind:'owned', storedPlatform:'web'}`, else
`{kind:'platform', storedPlatform:p}`. Keep both anyway: `kind` is the
AUTHORIZATION discriminator (and tells you whether `user_id` holds a Lobu user id
or a platform user id — the column is polymorphic). Collapsing it would spread
`platform !== 'web'` as an access predicate across six read sites, which is
[[feedback_text_matcher_is_never_the_boundary]].

Optional hardening: `CHECK ((kind = 'owned') = (platform = 'web')) NOT VALID`.
**Only add it if public/embedded web chat is NOT coming** — an anonymous
end-user web widget would be `platform='web'` but not `kind='owned'`. Also
verify the 1:1 holds across existing prod rows first; `conversations` is not
MCP-queryable so this was never checked.

Traced #3 — your fix is right, and it needs a route that doesn't exist yet.

`authCtx.agentId` **is** set, by `syncAgentBinding` (`mcp-handler.ts:842`), from `authCtx.requestedAgentId`. But that comes from the `x-lobu-agent-id` **header** or a JSON body field (`:421`, `:452`) — never the URL. The MCP mounts are only:

```
/mcp        /mcp/        /mcp/:orgSlug        /mcp/:orgSlug/
```

No agent segment. So no hosted client sends an agent, `requestedAgentId` is null, `syncAgentBinding` sets `agentId = null`, and `touchClientActivity` skips `last_agent_id` — which is exactly why it's NULL on all 19 prod rows. Not a bug; an opt-in nobody opts into.

Your proposal works as `/mcp/:orgSlug/:agentId` → `requestedAgentId` → existing `syncAgentBinding` (which already validates the agent exists in the org and errors cleanly if not) → `last_agent_id` gets written → `client` rows become agent-scopable. And since MCP binding is attribution, not authorization, adding it to the URL grants nothing — no authz risk.

name: reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution
description: "How an MCP client is identified (6 signals on oauth_clients + events.client_id), the display-name precedence conflict between two surfaces, and the fact that conversations carries NO client attribution — measured on prod 2026-07-30"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:10:57.248Z
---

## ChatGPT DOES create conversations — I was wrong twice

Measured on prod 2026-07-30. Do not repeat the claim that MCP clients only call
read tools; it is false.

```
ChatGPT | run_sdk 498 · query_sql 123 · query_sdk 32 · search_sdk 28 · search_memory 6 · save_memory 2
Claude  | run_sdk 1244 · query_sql 1224 · …
```

Of ChatGPT's `run_sdk` calls, **13 are `conversations.send`** — real agent
conversations. One is live in the listing right now:
`personal-agent_8a2D2Yb…_8dc12bdd…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5`, surfaced as
`{"id":"mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5","platform":"web"}`. ChatGPT's dominant SDK path
is `operations.execute` (539) — it drives the Chrome extension.

Method that works: `events` JOIN `oauth_clients` on `e.client_id`, then
`jsonb_array_elements(payload_data->'sdk_call_trace')` for `path` and `args`.
`conversations` itself is NOT in the MCP query allowlist.

## The six identity signals

Five on `oauth_clients`, one per-invocation:

| signal | when written | ChatGPT's value |
|---|---|---|
| `client_name` | DCR registration | `ChatGPT` |
| `metadata.last_client_info.name/title` | MCP `initialize`, per session | `openai-mcp` |
| `metadata.last_user_agent` | HTTP header | `openai-mcp/1.0.0` |
| `software_id` / `software_version` | DCR software statement | null |
| `redirect_uris` host | OAuth callback | `chatgpt.com` |
| `events.client_id` | every tool call | the only PER-INVOCATION signal |

Also `metadata.last_capabilities` — ChatGPT alone declares `openai/visibility`
and `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. `recordMcpClientActivity`
(`mcp-handler.ts:619` → `touchClientActivity`) writes the first three on every
authenticated request.

## Two surfaces disagree on the name

`client-routes.ts:258` uses `clientInfo.name || client_name` — clientInfo WINS.
`client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite.
**5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered as**, because
clientInfo reflects the process driving the connection, not the app:

```
Owletto for Mac → claude-code   (×3)
Lobu CLI        → claude-code
Claude          → claude-code
```

Trustworthy identity = `redirect_uris` host + `software_id` (can't be
self-reported away). `clientInfo` answers "what is driving it" — a different
question worth its own field, not an override.

## The attribution gap

`events.client_id` knows. **`conversations` does not** — the write path stores
`kind='owned'` → `platform:'web'` and drops the client. So ChatGPT, Claude, the
CLI and the browser all land in one undifferentiated bucket, and no query can
separate them. This is why there is no ChatGPT icon in Recent, and it is the same
missing field as the shared-thread attribution gap. Fix = `conversations.client_id`
written where the run is minted.

## last_seen_at exists; agent scoping does not

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is live on all 19 prod rows (Claude 17:43,
ChatGPT 17:10 on 2026-07-30) — the MCP equivalent of
`watchers.last_run_completed_at` already exists, no migration needed.

But `metadata.last_agent_id` is **NULL on all 19 rows** — `touchClientActivity`
only sets it `if (params.agentId)` and `authCtx.agentId` is evidently unset on
these requests. `client-routes.ts:255` filters
`if (agentId && assignedAgentId !== agentId) return null`, so that agent filter
currently drops every client. Per-agent MCP client rows need that write fixed
first; root cause not yet traced.

Related: [[project_recent_feed_unified]],
[[project_mcp_clients_as_external_agents]],
[[reference_behavior_conversation_id_is_client_forgeable]].

name: reference_conversation_id_is_a_session_key
description: "Why conversations has both conversation_id and thread_id — the web conversation_id is really a BullMQ/session/SSE key, so thread_id exists to pull a routable identity back out of it; conversation branching (parent_*) is designed but unbuilt"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:11:24.004Z
---

## The two ids

```
conversation_id: REDACTED…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5
thread_id:       mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5
```

|              | owned / web                        | platform                  |
|--------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| id shape     | `{agent}_{user}_{org}_{suffix}`    | `slack:D095U1QV667`       |
| separator    | `_` (BullMQ job ids ban `:`)       | `:`                       |
| `thread_id`  | the suffix                         | **null**                  |
| routes as    | `/chat/c/{threadId}`               | `/conversations/{conversationId}` |

`thread_id` was added by `20260727150000_conversations_thread_id.sql` to stop
reconstructing the route segment from `conversation_id` on every list read —
the same materialize-don't-derive instinct as
[[project_behavior_listing_column]].

## Why the web id is packed

`agent.ts:~898`: `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` is a GLOBAL constant, so without userId +
org baked in, two tenants could collide on one conversation id and resume each
other's session. The same string is simultaneously the BullMQ job id, the
session-store key, and the SSE owner-routing key.

**That is the debt: conversation identity is welded to the machine session key.**
`thread_id` is the patch that pulls a user-facing identity back out. Identical
conflation to `{agentId}_watcher_<id>_run_<runId>`, where run identity was welded
to listing identity. If a conversation had its own opaque primary identity and
the session key merely referenced it, `thread_id` would not exist, both routing
rules would collapse into one, and branching would have something stable to point
at. NOT worth refactoring now — that packed id is parsed by the MCP
unattended-tool gate, drives worker dispatch + SSE routing, and is guarded by the
sdk-e2e gate. Branching will force the issue.

## thread_id gates listability

The `conversations_fill_thread_id` trigger only fills when the id matches the
exact `{agent}_{user}_{org}_` prefix; otherwise NULL. `agent-thread-list.ts:221`
skips any owned row without one. **So an MCP client that invents its own
`conversationId` in a non-packed shape gets a working conversation that never
appears in Recent** — consistent with `e2e-conversation-ms28twyo` (bare custom
id) being absent from the prod listing while `mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5` (packed) is
present.

## Nesting

Platform ids already encode `{platform}:{channel}:{thread}` — `isConversationVisible`
splits on `:` and takes `parts[1]` as the channel for the ACL. So container→leaf
nesting exists, but only as string structure.

Modelled lineage does NOT exist. The original migration deferred it explicitly —
"branch lineage (`parent_*`) columns are introduced by the follow-ups that
actually read/write them" — and no conversations migration since adds it
(`sandbox_pin`, `thread_id`, `is_direct` only). Matches
[[project_home_chat_conversation_branching_arch]] (fork unbuilt).

## kind vs platform

`kind` is 100% derivable from `platform` today — `classifyConversation` is the
sole writer: `platform === 'api'` → `{kind:'owned', storedPlatform:'web'}`, else
`{kind:'platform', storedPlatform:p}`. Keep both anyway: `kind` is the
AUTHORIZATION discriminator (and tells you whether `user_id` holds a Lobu user id
or a platform user id — the column is polymorphic). Collapsing it would spread
`platform !== 'web'` as an access predicate across six read sites, which is
[[feedback_text_matcher_is_never_the_boundary]].

--
-- It was also unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
-- runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. 22 of 26 Behavior rows
-- observed on one prod agent were archived Behaviors it could never drop.
--
-- The fix is one column on the Behavior itself, not a row in another table.
-- `watchers` is a bounded config table, so `status` and `name` are read live at
-- listing time — which is why archive and rename need no synchronisation at all.
ALTER TABLE public.watchers
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_run_completed_at timestamptz;

-- Serves the listing read exactly: equality on (organization_id, agent_id),
-- ordered by the timestamp, with the two filters folded into the predicate.
-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation -- watchers is ~60 rows in prod; dbmate wraps this migration in a transaction, where CONCURRENTLY is not permitted
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS watchers_agent_recent
  ON public.watchers (organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status = 'active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL;

-- One-time backfill. This is the aggregation the read path is losing —
-- appropriate here (offline, once) and forbidden on a request path. Without it
-- every Behavior would be missing from the sidebar until its next completed run,
-- which is the failure mode `conversations.is_direct` shipped with.
--
-- Reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`: grouping on a real FK lets this
-- use `idx_runs_watcher_id (watcher_id) WHERE watcher_id IS NOT NULL`, where
-- parsing conversation ids out of transcript history would force the same
-- unindexable scan this change exists to delete.
UPDATE public.watchers w
SET last_run_completed_at = mx.last_at
FROM (
  SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) AS last_at
  FROM public.runs
  WHERE run_type = 'behavior'
    AND status = 'completed'
    AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL
    AND completed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY watcher_id
) mx
WHERE w.id = mx.watcher_id
  AND w.last_run_completed_at IS DISTINCT FROM mx.last_at;

Prerequisite for [[project_recent_feed_unified]]. Worktree
`.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows`, branch `feat/behavior-listing-rows`,
PORT 9186. **Two commits exist (34f1d50f4, 7953833cb) and are UNPUSHED — reset
them; the approach they implement was rejected.**

## The bug

`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
grows with run history forever.

Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
4 active / 56 archived org-wide).

## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)

Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.

## ACCEPTED approach

One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.

- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
  is ~60 rows in prod)
- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.

**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.

## Keep from the rejected branch

The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
assertion holds under either design; proved red against
`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.

## Gotchas hit

- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated
  (`dropdb/createdb lobu_test` + `CREATE EXTENSION vector, cube, earthdistance`).
- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.

## Unverified

Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
shipping the backfill**.

content.text:
You're right that `events.client_id` exists — I checked whether it's reachable, and it isn't, at least not cheaply.

`events` has `client_id` and `run_id` but **no conversation column**. The audit rows I sampled carry `agent_id`, `tool_name`, `mcp_session_id` in metadata — no conversation id. The conversation only appears buried inside the call trace:

```
payload_data -> 'sdk_call_trace' -> 0 -> 'args' -> 0 ->> 'conversation_id'
```

inside a JSONB **array**. And `runs` has `created_by_user_id` but no `client_id` at all, so it can't bridge either — its conversation link is also JSONB (`action_input->>'conversationId'`).

So "which client created this conversation?" today is a three-hop join through two JSONB paths across `events` and `runs`, both append-only and unbounded, with no index that helps. On the conversation-view render, that's exactly the aggregation the invariant you just set forbids. `mcp_sessions` doesn't rescue it either — it has `client_id` but no conversation id, and it's purged on expiry.

So `conversations.client_id` isn't a new idea, it's the **same pattern we just shipped for Behaviors**: the fact is known at write time, at the one place the run is minted, so store it on the row you'll read instead of reconstructing it from history.

One thing worth deciding explicitly, since it's the real modelling question: a conversation can have **several** clients over its life — ChatGPT starts it, you continue in the browser, Claude Code adds a turn. A single column can't hold all of them. My read is that it should mean **the client that created it, first-writer-wins** (same `COALESCE(existing, excluded)` rule as `is_direct`), because that's what "this conversation is from ChatGPT" in the composer slot actually claims, and it's stable for the row's lifetime. Per-turn attribution stays on `events.client_id`, where it already works and where the Client apps timeline reads it.

Nothing moves off `events` — this is additive and answers a different question.

**Confidence: high (~90).** The column lists are read from the baseline schema and the metadata shape from live prod audit rows. The one gap: I sampled `run_sdk` audit events specifically, so I can't rule out some other event type carrying a conversation id in metadata — worth a check before building, though it wouldn't change the conclusion since it'd still be a JSONB scan over `events`.

Want me to keep `client_id` on `conversations` with creator semantics, or would you rather it be nullable-and-multi (a join table) so a conversation can list every client that touched it?

**Union. Nothing consolidates into `conversations`.** Sorry — I flip-flopped mid-way and that's what lost you.

Three sources, each stays in its own table, joined only at read time:

| Recent row | comes from | ordering column | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| conversation (web, slack, telegram…) | `conversations` | `last_activity_at` | already exists |
| behavior | `watchers` | `last_run_completed_at` | **just shipped, `bf0cc78c6`** |
| client | `oauth_clients` | `metadata.last_seen_at` | already exists, no change needed |

`/workspace/recent` does a four-branch `UNION ALL` over those with a per-branch `LIMIT`. That's it. No table absorbs another.

**What changed my mind mid-conversation:** I first built Behaviors *into* `conversations` (a `behavior:<id>` row, `kind='behavior'`). You pushed back, and you were right — it needed a trigger, three leak guards, and a lifecycle sync, all defending against problems the shape created. That approach is dead and the code is reverted. So the label "this conversation is from ChatGPT" would be claiming more than the data supports. It tells you *who typed*, not *what the conversation is* — and the owner is already recorded, because `user_id` is the Lobu user whose OAuth token ChatGPT is acting under.

## E2E: what happens when you open the app

**Writes — all four already happen, none are new except the one I shipped:**

| event | writer | lands in |
|---|---|---|
| you send a browser message | `message-consumer.ts:493` `upsertConversation` | `conversations.last_activity_at` |
| a Slack/Telegram message arrives | same | `conversations` + `is_direct` |
| a Behavior run completes | `transcript-routes.ts` `stampBehaviorLastRun` | `watchers.last_run_completed_at` ← **PR 1** |
| any MCP request | `mcp-handler.ts:619` `touchClientActivity` | `oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` |

**Read — one request replaces the current per-agent fan-out:**

```
sidebar mounts
  └─ GET /lobu/api/v1/workspace/recent?limit=20
       ├─ resolveChannelVisibility(org, agents, user)   → visible channel keys (bounded)
       └─ UNION ALL, each branch LIMIT 20
            conversations  kind='owned'    AND user_id = me
            conversations  kind='platform' AND channel key = ANY($visibleKeys)
            watchers       status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL
            oauth_clients  organization_id = $org
          ORDER BY lastActivityAt DESC LIMIT 20
  └─ render: type='conversation' → platformIcon(platform)
             type='behavior'     → ListChecks  → /behaviors/$id
             type='client'       → AppWindow   → client detail (Revoke lives here)
```

## Gaps

**1 — Client rows will monopolise Recent.** This is the one that breaks the feature. `last_seen_at` updates on *every* MCP request, so during any session the connected client is permanently the newest thing in the workspace. Claude's stamp moved to 17:43 while I was working; ChatGPT's to 17:10. With 19 clients sorted by recency they'd occupy the top of the list continuously and push conversations out — the same "Behaviors drown everything" failure, but constant rather than occasional. Recency sorting is simply wrong for a signal that fires on every tool call. Options: give clients their own capped section, bucket `last_seen_at` to the hour, or exclude clients from the default view and surface them only under `filter=client`. **Needs your call before I build it.**

**2 — Channel fence vs per-branch LIMIT.** Fencing in TS after a `LIMIT 20` under-fills the page and makes `counts.platform` wrong. The visible-key set has to go into SQL as a `text[]` predicate — and that's the `fetch_types:false` raw-array trap, so `pgTextArray`, not a bare array.

**3 — `counts` costs four more queries.** Exact totals mean counting each branch separately, and the platform count must respect the fence. All are index-only scans, but it doubles the query count per render. Alternative: cap at "99+".

**4 — Client rows can't be agent-scoped.** `last_agent_id` is NULL on all 19 prod rows. `&agentId=` will silently drop every client until `/mcp/:orgSlug/:agentId` ships.

**5 — Agent deletion orphans rows.** `agents.delete` is live (ChatGPT called it 7 times). I found no cleanup of `conversations` or `watchers` on agent delete — only `entity-management.ts:1104` deleting watchers for an entity. So Recent can list a conversation whose agent no longer exists, and the link 404s. Needs verifying properly; if confirmed it's pre-existing, not caused by this work.

**6 — Cursor ties across namespaces.** Keyset on `(lastActivityAt, id)` where ids come from three namespaces (`watcher_71`, `slack:D…`, `mcp_client_…`). Same-millisecond ties need a deterministic tiebreak applied identically in SQL and in the cursor encoder, or pagination can skip or repeat rows.

**7 — Two consumers, one endpoint.** The sidebar moves to `/workspace/recent`, but `/threads?scope=all` still backs the per-agent conversation list. Don't delete it with the sidebar hook.

**8 — Revoke permission.** Today: any member sees the app list, only admins revoke. That gating has to move with it to the client detail view.

**9 — Behaviors are invisible until their first completed run** (`last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`). Matches the old behaviour exactly, so not a regression — but if you'd rather a newly created Behavior appear immediately, that's a different predicate.

**Confidence: high** on 1, 2, 4 — all measured this session (the `last_seen_at` churn, the fence logic, the NULL `last_agent_id`). Medium on 5; I grepped for cleanup and found none, but absence needs the `origin/main` check before I call it real. 3, 6, 8, 9 are design consequences, not findings.

Gap 1 is the blocker. Tell me how you want client rows to behave and I'll build the endpoint; the rest I can resolve as I go.

New AGENTS.md hard invariant (committed on `feat/behavior-listing-rows`):
**request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT ON` /
per-row `regexp_*` / leading-wildcard `LIKE` over `events`,
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls` on a user-facing read path.

`oauth_clients`) are fine to aggregate.

[[project_behavior_listing_column]]) and `client-session-routes.ts:76`
(`GROUP BY metadata->>'mcp_session_id'` over `current_event_records`) — PR 2.

## Contract

```
GET /lobu/api/v1/workspace/recent
  ?filter=web|slack|telegram|whatsapp|discord|behavior|client   repeatable; omit ⇒ all
  &agentId=<id>    repeatable; omit ⇒ all agents
  &limit=20 (max 100)  &cursor=<keyset on (lastActivityAt, id)>
```

Payload uses TWO fields — **`type` says what the row is, `platform` says which
external surface, null when there isn't one.** `platform` alone was rejected
("behavior is not a platform"); `trigger`/`origin`/`kind`/`source` were all
rejected as already-taken (see below).

```jsonc
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "slack", "conversationId": "slack:D095…" }
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "web",   "threadId": "mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5" }
{ "type": "behavior",     "platform": null,    "behaviorId": 71 }
{ "type": "client",       "platform": null,    "clientId": "mcp_client_8hOPs3…" }
```

Server resolves the flat filter as `type === 'conversation' ? platform : type`.
Response also carries `counts` per filter value — chips need totals, and a
truncated page gives wrong ones.

**Name collisions that forced `type`** (all verified in-repo/prod):
`trigger` = `watchers.triggers`; `origin` = `events.origin_type`, a
connector-owned open set with **84 distinct values in prod**; `kind` =
`conversations.kind` (owned/platform); `source` = `watchers.sources`.

## SQL shape

Four branches, `UNION ALL`, **each with its own `LIMIT $n`** so the union is at
most 4n rows regardless of table size; outer `ORDER BY … LIMIT $n`.
`conversations_listing` already indexes `(org, agent, last_activity_at DESC)
WHERE archived_at IS NULL`; `oauth_clients` is 19 rows.

**Trap:** the channel ACL fence is applied in TS today (`isConversationVisible`).
With per-branch LIMIT that under-fills the page and makes `counts.platform`
wrong. Resolve visible channel keys first (bounded), pass them into the platform
branch as a `text[]` predicate — and that needs `pgTextArray`, see
[[feedback_pg_array_any_fetch_types]].

`client.workspace.recent({ filter?, agent_id?, limit, cursor })`, read access,
same union behind both surfaces. Today only `client.conversations.list({agent_id})`
exists — conversations only, per agent, can't answer "recent activity".

---
name: project_recent_feed_unified
description: "DESIGN (approved 2026-07-30, unbuilt) — one workspace-level /recent feed unioning conversations + Behaviors + MCP clients; API uses type + nullable platform with a flat filter param; replaces the per-agent /threads?scope=all fan-out and the /connectors/apps page"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:52:41.786Z
---

Approved design, **not yet built**. Grew out of "why don't I see Recent?" →
[[project_dm_conversation_visibility]] → the archived-Behaviors bug.

## The rule this obeys

New AGENTS.md hard invariant (committed on `feat/behavior-listing-rows`):
**request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT ON` /
per-row `regexp_*` / leading-wildcard `LIKE` over `events`,
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls` on a user-facing read path.
Materialize at WRITE time; run the one-time aggregation in a migration.
Bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`,
`oauth_clients`) are fine to aggregate.

Two known violations: `agent-thread-list.ts` (being fixed, see
[[project_behavior_listing_column]]) and `client-session-routes.ts:76`
(`GROUP BY metadata->>'mcp_session_id'` over `current_event_records`) — PR 2.

## Contract

```
GET /lobu/api/v1/workspace/recent
  ?filter=web|slack|telegram|whatsapp|discord|behavior|client   repeatable; omit ⇒ all
  &agentId=<id>    repeatable; omit ⇒ all agents
  &limit=20 (max 100)  &cursor=<keyset on (lastActivityAt, id)>
```

Payload uses TWO fields — **`type` says what the row is, `platform` says which
external surface, null when there isn't one.** `platform` alone was rejected
("behavior is not a platform"); `trigger`/`origin`/`kind`/`source` were all
rejected as already-taken (see below).

```jsonc
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "slack", "conversationId": "slack:D095…" }
{ "type": "conversation", "platform": "web",   "threadId": "mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5" }
{ "type": "behavior",     "platform": null,    "behaviorId": 71 }
{ "type": "client",       "platform": null,    "clientId": "mcp_client_8hOPs3…" }
```

Server resolves the flat filter as `type === 'conversation' ? platform : type`.
Response also carries `counts` per filter value — chips need totals, and a
truncated page gives wrong ones.

**Name collisions that forced `type`** (all verified in-repo/prod):
`trigger` = `watchers.triggers`; `origin` = `events.origin_type`, a
connector-owned open set with **84 distinct values in prod**; `kind` =
`conversations.kind` (owned/platform); `source` = `watchers.sources`.

## SQL shape

Four branches, `UNION ALL`, **each with its own `LIMIT $n`** so the union is at
most 4n rows regardless of table size; outer `ORDER BY … LIMIT $n`.
`conversations_listing` already indexes `(org, agent, last_activity_at DESC)
WHERE archived_at IS NULL`; `oauth_clients` is 19 rows.

**Trap:** the channel ACL fence is applied in TS today (`isConversationVisible`).
With per-branch LIMIT that under-fills the page and makes `counts.platform`
wrong. Resolve visible channel keys first (bounded), pass them into the platform
branch as a `text[]` predicate — and that needs `pgTextArray`, see
[[feedback_pg_array_any_fetch_types]].

## Also exposed via run_sdk

`client.workspace.recent({ filter?, agent_id?, limit, cursor })`, read access,
same union behind both surfaces. Today only `client.conversations.list({agent_id})`
exists — conversations only, per agent, can't answer "recent activity".

## `/connectors/apps` gets deleted

Its list is redundant once `client` rows exist. **But it is the ONLY consumer of
`useRevokeMcpClient` in the SPA** — deleting it naively removes the sole way to
disconnect ChatGPT/Claude. Decision: Revoke moves into the **conversation view's
composer slot** — `agent-thread.tsx:145` already branches
`readOnly ? footer : <ChatComposer/>`, so a client-attribution panel ("this
conversation is from ChatGPT" + info + Revoke) drops into that existing slot.
Requires conversation→client attribution first, see
[[reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution]].

Inbound refs to sweep before deleting: `app-sidebar.tsx:419` (nav item),
`client-sessions-timeline.tsx:63` (link), `all-routes.test.tsx`, and
`group-clients.test.ts` which imports `groupClients` from the route file.
Docs/help text not yet swept.

## Client rows must NOT be recency-sorted with everything else

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is bumped on EVERY authenticated MCP
request (`touchClientActivity`), so a connected client is permanently the newest
thing in the workspace — measured live: Claude 17:43, ChatGPT 17:10 while
working. Plain recency sorting would let 19 client rows sit at the top forever
and squeeze conversations out — the "Behaviors drown everything" failure, but
continuous. **DECIDED: clients get their own capped section (~3 rows); they do
not compete in the main recency ordering.**

## conversations.client_id — DROPPED, with an expiry condition

Dropped 2026-07-30. A Lobu conversation is a conversation with a LOBU AGENT.
When ChatGPT calls `conversations.send` there is no ChatGPT content in the row —
just the prompt it passed and the agent's reply. Labelling it "from ChatGPT"
claims more than the data supports, `user_id` already records the owning Lobu
user, and `events.client_id` already carries per-invocation attribution at the
correct grain (a conversation can be touched by several clients).

**Revisit when the inference proxy / SDK starts populating external clients'
own transcripts** (user's plan, 2026-07-30). Once a conversation actually
contains the client's turns, `client_id` stops being a mislabel and the
composer-slot attribution panel becomes accurate again. Until then Revoke lives
on a **client detail view** reached from the `client` row, NOT in the
conversation composer slot — that earlier plan depended on client_id.

## Ordering

1. [[project_behavior_listing_column]] — prerequisite, unblocked.
2. `conversations.client_id` attribution.
3. `/workspace/recent` + `client.workspace.recent`.
4. SPA switches Recent to it; `/connectors/apps` deleted in the SAME PR so the
   page and its replacement land together.
5. PR 2 — `client-session-routes.ts` de-aggregation.

Prerequisite for [[project_recent_feed_unified]]. Worktree
`.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows`, branch `feat/behavior-listing-rows`,
PORT 9186.

**STATUS 2026-07-30: REWRITTEN AND COMMITTED as `bf0cc78c6`, still UNPUSHED.**
6 files: AGENTS.md, `db/migrations/20260730210000_watchers_last_run_completed_at.sql`,
`transcript-routes.ts` (`stampBehaviorLastRun`), `agent-thread-list.ts` (union
from watchers), and 2 test files. All gates green; red→green re-proved against
`origin/main`'s read path; test DB verified free of the rejected design's
trigger/CHECK. NOT yet booted against a live Behavior run — that and
`make review` are what remain before pushing.

## The bug

`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
grows with run history forever.

Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
4 active / 56 archived org-wide).

## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)

Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.

## ACCEPTED approach

One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.

- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
  is ~60 rows in prod)
- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.

**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.

## Keep from the rejected branch

The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
assertion holds under either design; proved red against
`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.

## Gotchas hit

- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated
  (`dropdb/createdb lobu_test` + `CREATE EXTENSION vector, cube, earthdistance`).
- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.

## Unverified

Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
shipping the backfill**.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. 3	description: "Booting a task worktree for browser/e2e testing: build-packages (not build), make dev serves only the API, the SPA is a separate vite with LOBU_API_PROXY, and how to drive an agent-attributed tool call without an LLM"
4	metadata:

7	  originSessionId: c3dc213c-a275-44a5-9345-8bf68a35760f
8	  modified: 2026-07-29T15:52:45.643Z
9	---
10	
11	The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.
12	
13	**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
14	`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].
15	
16	**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.
17	
18	**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
19	```
20	cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
21	  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
22	```
23	`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.
24	
25	**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
26	Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
27	```
28	/api/auth-config       -> 200
29	/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
30	```
31	See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.
32	
33	**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).
34	
35	**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
36	```
37	cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
38	  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
39	```
40	
41	**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
42	`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. Skipping the handshake returns `Bad Request: Server not initialized`.
43	
44	Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

description: "Booting a task worktree for browser/e2e testing: build-packages (not build), make dev serves only the API, the SPA is a separate vite with LOBU_API_PROXY, and how to drive an agent-attributed tool call without an LLM"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c3dc213c-a275-44a5-9345-8bf68a35760f
  modified: 2026-07-29T15:52:45.643Z
---

The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.

**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].

**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.

**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
```
cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
```
`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.

**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
```
/api/auth-config       -> 200
/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
```
See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).

**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
```
cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
```

**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. Skipping the handshake returns `Bad Request: Server not initialized`.

Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows and those predicates are unindexable, so the cost climbs forever while the answer stays the same. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.
