#!/bin/bash
# End-to-end demo: a Behavior's completed run stamps watchers.last_run_completed_at,
# and the agent listing reads it back by index instead of aggregating run history.
set -u
WT=/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows
SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41/scratchpad
DB="psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -d lobu_feat_behavior_listing_rows"
API=http://127.0.0.1:9186
COOKIE=$SCRATCH/cookies.txt

B=$'\033[1m'; G=$'\033[32m'; Y=$'\033[33m'; C=$'\033[36m'; R=$'\033[31m'; N=$'\033[0m'
say() { printf "\n${B}${C}%s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 1; }
run() { printf "${Y}\$ %s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 0.6; eval "$@"; sleep 1.2; }

say "1. Create a Behavior through the real API"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"create\",\"slug\":\"quarterly-check\",\"name\":\"Quarterly Check\",\"prompt\":\"Summarise.\",\"agent_id\":\"owletto-default\"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool | head -4"

BID=$($DB -tAc "select id from watchers where name='Quarterly Check'")

say "2. Trigger it. One Behavior execution writes TWO runs — this is what the bug hinged on."
RUN=$(curl -s -b "$COOKIE" -X POST "$API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"action\":\"trigger\",\"behavior_id\":\"$BID\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["run_id"])')
printf "${Y}\$ trigger behavior %s -> behavior run %s${N}\n" "$BID" "$RUN"
until [ -n "$($DB -tAc "select 1 from runs where id=$RUN and status in ('completed','failed','cancelled')")" ]; do sleep 2; done

CONV="owletto-default_watcher_${BID}_run_${RUN}"
run "$DB -c \"select id, run_type, action_input->>'conversationId' as conversation_id from runs where id=$RUN or action_input->>'conversationId'='$CONV' order by id limit 3\""

printf "${B}The conversation id packs the ${G}behavior${N}${B} run id (%s).${N}\n" "$RUN"
printf "${B}The worker token + checkpoint body carry the ${G}chat_message${N}${B} run id — a different number.${N}\n"
sleep 2.5

TURN=$($DB -tAc "select id from runs where action_input->>'conversationId'='$CONV' and action_input ? 'agentId' order by id limit 1")

say "3. A FAILED checkpoint must not count as activity"
run "ENCRYPTION_KEY=\$(grep -m1 '^ENCRYPTION_KEY=' $WT/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\"') \
  node $WT/e2e-post-snapshot.mjs '$CONV' $TURN failed"
run "$DB -c \"select id, name, status, last_run_completed_at from watchers where id=$BID\""

say "4. Now the COMPLETED checkpoint — the same request the worker sends"
run "ENCRYPTION_KEY=\$(grep -m1 '^ENCRYPTION_KEY=' $WT/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\"') \
  node $WT/e2e-post-snapshot.mjs '$CONV' $TURN completed"
run "$DB -c \"select id, name, status, last_run_completed_at from watchers where id=$BID\""

say "5. The listing endpoint reads that column back — no GROUP BY over run history"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -m json.tool"

say "6. Archive it. The old read-time derive could never drop an archived Behavior:"
say "   archiving does not unmake its past runs. 22 of 26 rows on prod were stuck this way."
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"delete\",\"behavior_ids\":[\"$BID\"]}' | python3 -m json.tool | head -6"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json;[print(\" -\", t[\"behaviorId\"], t[\"title\"]) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)[\"threads\"]]'"

printf "\n${B}${G}Gone from the listing — while the row keeps its stamp.${N}\n"
printf "${B}status and name are read live off watchers, so archive and rename need no sync at all.${N}\n\n"
sleep 2

#!/bin/bash
# End-to-end demo: a Behavior's completed run stamps watchers.last_run_completed_at,
# and the agent listing reads it back by index instead of aggregating run history.
set -u
WT=/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows
SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41/scratchpad
DB="psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -d lobu_feat_behavior_listing_rows"
API=http://127.0.0.1:9186
COOKIE=$SCRATCH/cookies.txt

B=$'\033[1m'; G=$'\033[32m'; Y=$'\033[33m'; C=$'\033[36m'; R=$'\033[31m'; N=$'\033[0m'
say() { printf "\n${B}${C}%s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 1; }
run() { printf "${Y}\$ %s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 0.6; eval "$@"; sleep 1.2; }

say "1. Create a Behavior through the real API"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"create\",\"slug\":\"quarterly-check\",\"name\":\"Quarterly Check\",\"prompt\":\"Summarise.\",\"agent_id\":\"owletto-default\"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool | head -4"

BID=$($DB -tAc "select id from watchers where name='Quarterly Check'")

say "2. Trigger it. One Behavior execution writes TWO runs — this is what the bug hinged on."
RUN=$(curl -s -b "$COOKIE" -X POST "$API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"action\":\"trigger\",\"behavior_id\":\"$BID\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["run_id"])')
printf "${Y}\$ trigger behavior %s -> behavior run %s${N}\n" "$BID" "$RUN"
until [ -n "$($DB -tAc "select 1 from runs where id=$RUN and status in ('completed','failed','cancelled')")" ]; do sleep 2; done

CONV="owletto-default_watcher_${BID}_run_${RUN}"
run "$DB -c \"select id, run_type, action_input->>'conversationId' as conversation_id from runs where id=$RUN or action_input->>'conversationId'='$CONV' order by id limit 3\""

printf "${B}The conversation id packs the ${G}behavior${N}${B} run id (%s).${N}\n" "$RUN"
printf "${B}The worker token + checkpoint body carry the ${G}chat_message${N}${B} run id — a different number.${N}\n"
sleep 2.5

TURN=$($DB -tAc "select id from runs where action_input->>'conversationId'='$CONV' and action_input ? 'agentId' order by id limit 1")

say "3. A FAILED checkpoint must not count as activity"
run "ENCRYPTION_KEY=\$(grep -m1 '^ENCRYPTION_KEY=' $WT/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\"') \
  node $WT/e2e-post-snapshot.mjs '$CONV' $TURN failed"
run "$DB -c \"select id, name, status, last_run_completed_at from watchers where id=$BID\""

say "4. Now the COMPLETED checkpoint — the same request the worker sends"
run "ENCRYPTION_KEY=\$(grep -m1 '^ENCRYPTION_KEY=' $WT/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\"') \
  node $WT/e2e-post-snapshot.mjs '$CONV' $TURN completed"
run "$DB -c \"select id, name, status, last_run_completed_at from watchers where id=$BID\""

say "5. The listing endpoint reads that column back — no GROUP BY over run history"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -m json.tool"

say "6. Archive it. The old read-time derive could never drop an archived Behavior:"
say "   archiving does not unmake its past runs. 22 of 26 rows on prod were stuck this way."
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"delete\",\"behavior_ids\":[\"$BID\"]}' | python3 -m json.tool | head -6"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json;[print(\" -\", t[\"behaviorId\"], t[\"title\"]) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)[\"threads\"]]'"

printf "\n${B}${G}Gone from the listing — while the row keeps its stamp.${N}\n"
printf "${B}status and name are read live off watchers, so archive and rename need no sync at all.${N}\n\n"
sleep 2

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

feat/behavior-listing-rows · verified on a booted server

Behaviors stop aggregating run history

Booting it caught a regression the whole test suite had agreed with. Here is what ran, and what it proved.

The original bug

The agent listing derived Behavior rows at read time — a leading-wildcard LIKE plus a per-row regexp_match and a GROUP BY over agent_transcript_snapshot, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable, and it grows with run history forever.

It was also unfixably stale. Archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past runs, so the query had nothing to filter on: 22 of the 26 Behavior rows on prod's personal-agent were archived Behaviors it could never drop.

The fix materialises the answer at write time — watchers.last_run_completed_at, stamped by the terminal checkpoint, read back by a partial index — and reads status and name live off the same row, so archive and rename need no synchronisation at all.

What booting caught

Executing one Behavior writes two rows in runs: the run_type='behavior' job, whose id is packed into the conversation id as _run_<id>, and the run_type='chat_message' turn the dispatcher queues for it — which is the id the worker token and the checkpoint body carry.

The committed guard required those two to be equal. They are never equal.

run idrun_typeaction_input → conversationId
224behavior—
225chat_messageowletto-default_watcher_6_run_224
227chat_messageowletto-default_watcher_6_run_224

The test fixture built the conversation id out of the same run id it put in the token, so the two id spaces coincided and the broken guard passed. Production has never once produced that shape.

Red → green, against the live server

The same request both times: a real worker token, the real POST /lobu/worker/transcript/snapshot route, the real database.

Committed code

Checkpoint accepted, snapshot written, Behavior never stamped — it would have vanished from the listing entirely.

200 {"id":1}

 id | name             | last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+----------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | NULL

After the fix

Identical request, identical data. The stamp lands on the snapshot's own timestamp.

200 {"id":1}

 id | name             | last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+----------------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | 2026-07-30 20:08:41.374+01

The full path, recorded

Create a Behavior through the API, trigger it, checkpoint it as the worker does, read it back through the listing endpoint, then archive it.

What each step proved

  • A failed checkpoint does not stamp. Only completed runs count as activity — the same filter the deleted aggregation used.
  • A completed checkpoint stamps the snapshot's own created_at, so the listed instant is identical to what the aggregation computed, just precomputed.
  • The listing endpoint returns Behaviors ordered by that column — a bounded index read on watchers, no history scan.
  • Archiving drops the row immediately while the stamp stays put. This is the prod bug: the old derive path could never do this.

Still owed

  • No LLM completed a run on this machine. Every provider key is exhausted — Anthropic out of credit, Z.ai weekly limit, Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on an unrelated tool-schema bug. Five real Behavior runs were dispatched and all five failed at the model. The checkpoint was therefore driven directly, which is the code under test; the model's output is not.
  • No UI in this branch consumes it. The sidebar that renders these rows lives on an unmerged owletto branch, so there is no screen to film here.
  • Prod backfill is unsized. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction and the runs row count has not been measured.

---
name: project_behavior_listing_column
description: "Behaviors leave the read-time aggregation for watchers.last_run_completed_at — the conversations-row approach was BUILT then REJECTED as over-engineered; branch feat/behavior-listing-rows needs a full rewrite (2 unpushed commits to reset)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:23:39.843Z
---

Prerequisite for [[project_recent_feed_unified]]. Worktree
`.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows`, branch `feat/behavior-listing-rows`,
PORT 9186.

**STATUS 2026-07-30: REWRITTEN AND COMMITTED as `bf0cc78c6`, still UNPUSHED.**
6 files: AGENTS.md, `db/migrations/20260730210000_watchers_last_run_completed_at.sql`,
`transcript-routes.ts` (`stampBehaviorLastRun`), `agent-thread-list.ts` (union
from watchers), and 2 test files. All gates green; red→green re-proved against
`origin/main`'s read path; test DB verified free of the rejected design's
trigger/CHECK. NOT yet booted against a live Behavior run — that and
`make review` are what remain before pushing.

## The bug

`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
grows with run history forever.

Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
4 active / 56 archived org-wide).

## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)

Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.

## ACCEPTED approach

One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.

- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
  is ~60 rows in prod)
- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.

**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.

## Keep from the rejected branch

The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
assertion holds under either design; proved red against
`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.

## Gotchas hit

- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated
  (`dropdb/createdb lobu_test` + `CREATE EXTENSION vector, cube, earthdistance`).
- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.

## Unverified

Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
shipping the backfill**.

---
name: reference_behavior_execution_writes_two_runs
description: "One Behavior execution writes TWO runs rows with different ids — the behavior job (packed into the conversation id as _run_<id>) and the chat_message turn (carried by the worker token and snapshot body); never compare the two"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
---

Measured live on `:9186`, 2026-07-30.

Triggering Behavior `<id>` creates:

1. `runs` row with `run_type='behavior'`, `watcher_id` set, payload in
   **`approved_input`**, `action_input` **NULL**. Its id is what gets packed into
   the conversation id: `<agentId>_watcher_<behaviorId>_run_<THIS id>`.
2. One or more `runs` rows with `run_type='chat_message'`, payload in
   **`action_input`** (`{agentId, conversationId}`). One of these is the queue row
   `MessageConsumer` claims, so **its** id is `token.runId` and the `runId` in the
   transcript-snapshot POST body.

Concretely: conversation `owletto-default_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under
`runId=112`.

Consequences:

- **Never compare `parseBehaviorRunConversationId(conv).runId` against the
  request/token `runId`.** Different id spaces; the comparison is never true.
  This silently killed `stampBehaviorLastRun` — see
  [[project_behavior_listing_column]].
- `isRunOwnedByJwtScope` (transcript-routes) reads **only `action_input`**, so it
  authorizes against the chat_message row. A `run_type='behavior'` row can never
  satisfy it.
- A test fixture that derives the conversation id from the same id it mints the
  token with collapses the two spaces and will pass against broken code. Insert
  both rows. [[feedback_test_the_shape_production_throws]]

Related: [[reference_conversation_id_is_a_session_key]] — `conversation_id` is a
session key, and this is a second way its embedded ids are not what they look
like.

content.text:
Let me give you the state of things while the fixer pass finishes.

**Booting it caught a real regression in my own change.** The committed version of `stampBehaviorLastRun` was dead code.

Executing one Behavior writes **two** rows in `runs`. The `run_type='behavior'` job is the one whose id gets packed into the conversation id as `_run_<id>`; the `run_type='chat_message'` turn the dispatcher queues for it is the one the worker token and the checkpoint body carry. Measured live: conversation `owletto-default_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under `runId=112`. The guard I kept from `review-fix` required those two to be equal, so it never fired — Behaviors would have disappeared from the listing entirely.

The unit test agreed with the bug, which is why nothing caught it: the fixture built the conversation id out of the same run id it minted the token with, collapsing two id spaces that production never collapses. Fixture now inserts both rows, and I mutation-tested it (broken guard → 1 fail).

Red→green on the booted server, same request both times:

| | committed | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| POST /worker/transcript/snapshot | `200 {"id":1}` | `200 {"id":1}` |
| `watchers.last_run_completed_at` | `NULL` | `2026-07-30 20:08:41.374+01` |

Then through the real listing endpoint: three Behaviors ordered by the stamp, and archiving one drops it while its stamp stays — the prod bug (22 of 26 rows stuck) actually fixed.

**Recording + write-up:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22

Two honest limits, both on the page. **No LLM completed a run here** — every provider key on this machine is exhausted (Anthropic no credit, Z.ai weekly limit, Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on an unrelated `reasoning_effort` + tools bug). Five real Behavior runs dispatched and all five died at the model, which incidentally proved the negative case. So I drove the checkpoint POST directly with a minted worker token — that route *is* the code under test; the model's output is not. And **no UI on this branch consumes `scope=all`** — the Recent sidebar is on the unmerged owletto branch, so there was no screen to film.

`make pre-pr` is clean and both affected test files pass (22 + 18).

6	- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
7	- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.
8	
9	## Hard invariants
10	- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
11	- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
12	- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
13	- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
14	- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
15	- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
16	- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
17	- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
18	  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
19	- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
20	- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
21	- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.

#!/bin/bash
# End-to-end: a completed Behavior run stamps watchers.last_run_completed_at at
# the database boundary, and the agent listing reads it back by index instead of
# aggregating run history.
set -u
WT=/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/behavior-listing-rows
SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41/scratchpad
DB="psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -d lobu_feat_behavior_listing_rows"
API=http://127.0.0.1:9186
COOKIE=$SCRATCH/cookies.txt
NAME="Quarterly Check"

B=$'\033[1m'; G=$'\033[32m'; Y=$'\033[33m'; C=$'\033[36m'; N=$'\033[0m'
say() { printf "\n${B}${C}%s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 1.1; }
run() { printf "${Y}\$ %s${N}\n" "$*"; sleep 0.6; eval "$@"; sleep 1.3; }

say "1. Create a Behavior through the real API"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"create\",\"slug\":\"quarterly-check\",\"name\":\"$NAME\",\"prompt\":\"Summarise.\",\"agent_id\":\"owletto-default\"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool | head -4"

BID=$($DB -tAc "select id from watchers where name='$NAME'")

say "2. Trigger a real run. It dispatches to the worker for real."
RUN=$(curl -s -b "$COOKIE" -X POST "$API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"action\":\"trigger\",\"behavior_id\":\"$BID\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["run_id"])')
printf "${Y}\$ trigger behavior %s  ->  run %s${N}\n" "$BID" "$RUN"
until [ -n "$($DB -tAc "select 1 from runs where id=$RUN and status in ('completed','failed','cancelled')")" ]; do sleep 2; done

say "   Every model provider on this machine is out of credit, so it FAILS —"
say "   which is the negative case worth seeing: a failed run is not activity."
run "$DB -c \"select id, status, left(coalesce(error_message,''),58) as error from runs where id=$RUN\""
run "$DB -c \"select id, name, status, last_run_completed_at from watchers where id=$BID\""

say "3. Now settle it the way a successful worker does — the real writer,"
say "   markWatcherRunCompleted(), issuing the same UPDATE production issues."
run "cd $WT/packages/server && DATABASE_URL=\"postgres://\$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_feat_behavior_listing_rows\" \
  PGSSLMODE=disable node ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx e2e-complete-run.ts $RUN 2>/dev/null"

printf "${B}The trigger on ${G}runs${N}${B} stamped ${G}watchers.last_run_completed_at${N}${B} in the same${N}\n"
printf "${B}transaction — keyed on ${G}runs.watcher_id${N}${B}, a real foreign key. No id parsing.${N}\n"
sleep 2.5

say "4. The listing endpoint reads that column back — no GROUP BY over history"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -m json.tool"

say "5. Archive it. The old read-time derive could never drop an archived"
say "   Behavior — archiving does not unmake its past runs."
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -X POST $API/api/e2e-proof/manage_behaviors -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"action\":\"delete\",\"behavior_ids\":[\"$BID\"]}' | python3 -m json.tool | head -6"
run "curl -s -b $COOKIE -H 'x-lobu-org: e2e-proof' '$API/lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json;[print(\" -\", t[\"behaviorId\"], t[\"title\"]) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)[\"threads\"]]'"

printf "\n${B}${G}Gone from the listing — and its stamp is still on the row.${N}\n"
printf "${B}status and name are read live off watchers, so archive and rename need no sync.${N}\n\n"
sleep 2

feat/behavior-listing-rows · verified on a booted server

Behaviors stop aggregating run history

Booting it killed two designs before one survived. Here is what ran, and what each step proved.

The original bug

The agent listing derived Behavior rows at read time — a leading-wildcard LIKE plus a per-row regexp_match and a GROUP BY over agent_transcript_snapshot, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable, and the scan grows with run history forever.

It was also unfixably stale. Archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past runs, so the query had nothing to filter on: 22 of the 26 Behavior rows on prod's personal-agent were archived Behaviors it could never drop.

The answer is to materialise it — watchers.last_run_completed_at, read back through a partial index — and to read status and name live off the same row, so archive and rename need no synchronisation at all. The open question was where the write happens.

First attempt, and what booting caught

The committed version stamped the column from the worker's transcript checkpoint, recovering the Behavior's id by parsing it out of the conversation id. On a booted server that turned out to be dead code.

Executing one Behavior writes two rows in runs: the run_type='behavior' job, whose id is packed into the conversation id as _run_<id>, and the run_type='chat_message' turn the dispatcher queues for it — which is the id the worker token and the checkpoint body carry.

run idrun_typeaction_input → conversationId
224behavior—
225chat_messageowletto-default_watcher_6_run_224
227chat_messageowletto-default_watcher_6_run_224

The guard required those two ids to be equal. They are never equal, so the stamp never fired and Behaviors would have vanished from the listing entirely.

The unit test agreed with the bug. Its fixture built the conversation id out of the same run id it minted the token with, collapsing two id spaces that production never collapses — so the broken guard passed.

Committed code

Checkpoint accepted, snapshot written, Behavior never stamped.

200 {"id":1}

 id | name             | last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+----------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | NULL

Guard removed

Identical request, identical data. The stamp lands.

200 {"id":1}

 id | name             | last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+----------------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | 2026-07-30 20:08:41.374+01

Second attempt, and why it is the one that ships

Deleting the guard made the checkpoint path work, but it left the design recovering a foreign key by parsing a string. The fixer pass moved the write to the database boundary instead: a trigger on runs that fires when a Behavior run reaches completed, keyed on runs.watcher_id — an actual foreign key.

That deletes the whole class of defect rather than the instance. There is no id to parse, so there are no two id spaces to confuse; and every writer that completes a run is covered, including old replicas mid-rolling-deploy, because the run transition and the stamp are one transaction.

The fixer could not run Postgres in its sandbox, so none of this was verified when it was written. It is verified here: the migration was re-applied to a freshly created database, and the stamp was driven by markWatcherRunCompleted() — the real production writer — not by hand-written SQL.

The full path, recorded

Create a Behavior through the API, trigger a real run, watch it fail at the model, then settle it the way a successful worker does, read it back through the listing endpoint, and archive it.

What each step proved

  • A failed run is not activity. Three real dispatched runs failed at the model and the column stayed NULL — the negative case, for free.
  • The real completion writer fires the trigger. markWatcherRunCompleted() sets status and completed_at on the row carrying watcher_id; the stamp lands on the same instant, in the same transaction.
  • The listing endpoint orders by that column — a bounded index read on watchers, no history scan.
  • Archiving drops the row immediately while the stamp stays put. This is the prod bug; the old derive path could never do it.
  • The tests fail without the trigger. Mutating the migration so the trigger cannot match drops three tests from pass to fail — they exercise the mechanism, not a hand-set value.

Still owed

  • No LLM completed a run on this machine. Every provider key is exhausted — Anthropic out of credit, Z.ai weekly limit, Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on an unrelated tool-schema bug. The completion transition was therefore invoked directly through the production function; the model's output is not what this change reads.
  • No UI on this branch consumes it. The sidebar that renders these rows lives on an unmerged owletto branch, so there is no screen to film here.
  • The prod backfill is unsized. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction and the runs row count has not been measured.

## Summary
- The agent listing derived Behavior rows at read time — leading-wildcard `LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over `agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable, over an append-only table, so the scan grows with run history forever.
- It was also unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past runs, so the query had nothing to filter on. **22 of 26 Behavior rows on prod's `personal-agent` were archived Behaviors it could never drop.**
- Materialize instead: `watchers.last_run_completed_at`, written by a trigger on `runs` when a Behavior run reaches `completed`, read back through a partial index. `status` and `name` are read live off the same row, so archive and rename need no synchronization — that is what fixes the stale rows.
- Adds the AGENTS.md invariant this obeys: request paths never aggregate history.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `agent-thread-list-scope-all.test.ts` 18/18 (vitest), `agent-transcript-snapshot.test.ts` 21/21 (bun)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval — n/a

### red → green

Booted on `:9186` against a freshly created database so the migration file itself ran.

**RED — three real Behavior runs dispatched to the worker.** Every model provider on this
machine is out of credit, so all three failed at the model. A failed run is not activity:

```
 id |       name       | status | last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+--------+-----------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | active |
  2 | Inbox Triage     | active |
  3 | Deal Watch       | active |
```

**GREEN — settle the run the way a successful worker does,** through the real production
writer `markWatcherRunCompleted()` (not hand-written SQL). The trigger stamps in the same
transaction, on the run's own `completed_at`:

```json
{ "run_id": 20, "status": "completed",
  "completed_at":          "2026-07-30T19:32:59.736Z",
  "behavior_id": 1, "name": "Morning Briefing",
  "last_run_completed_at": "2026-07-30T19:32:59.736Z" }
```

**The listing endpoint reads it back,** ordered by the stored stamp
(`GET /lobu/api/v1/agents/owletto-default/history/threads?scope=all`):

```
 - 3 Deal Watch
 - 2 Inbox Triage
 - 1 Morning Briefing
```

**Archiving drops the row immediately** — the behaviour the old derive path could never
produce — while the stamp stays on the row:

```
 id |       name       |  status  |     last_run_completed_at
----+------------------+----------+-------------------------------
  1 | Morning Briefing | active   | 2026-07-30 20:32:59.736709+01
  2 | Inbox Triage     | archived | 2026-07-30 20:33:10.386207+01
  3 | Deal Watch       | active   | 2026-07-30 20:33:11.970606+01

listing:  - 3 Deal Watch
          - 1 Morning Briefing
```

**Mutation check.** Editing the migration so the trigger's `WHEN` clause cannot match takes
`agent-thread-list-scope-all.test.ts` from 18 pass to `3 failed | 15 passed` — the tests
exercise the mechanism, not a hand-set column value.

## Notes

Recorded walkthrough and the full write-up, including a first design that booting killed:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22

An earlier version of this branch stamped the column from the worker's transcript checkpoint,
parsing the Behavior id out of the conversation id. Booting showed it was dead code: one
Behavior execution writes **two** `runs` rows — the `run_type='behavior'` job, whose id is
packed into the conversation id as `_run_<id>`, and the `run_type='chat_message'` turn the
dispatcher queues for it, which is the id the worker token and checkpoint body carry
(measured: conversation `…_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under `runId=112`). A guard
requiring the two to be equal could never fire. The trigger keys on `runs.watcher_id`
instead, so there is no id to parse and no id space to confuse.

**Not verified:** no LLM completed a run locally (Anthropic out of credit, Z.ai weekly limit,
Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on an unrelated `reasoning_effort` + function-tools
incompatibility), so the completion transition was invoked through the production function
rather than by a worker finishing normally. No UI on this branch consumes `scope=all` — the
sidebar that renders these rows is on an unmerged owletto branch. The prod `runs` row count
has not been measured, so the backfill's transaction time is unsized.
EOF

content.text:
PR is up: **https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2370**. `make review` is running. Here's where things landed — the design changed after my last message, and that's the important part.

The fixer pass moved the write from the application to a **trigger on `runs`**, keyed on `runs.watcher_id` — a real foreign key. That deletes the class of defect rather than the instance I'd found: there's no id to parse, so the two-id-space confusion can't occur, and every completion writer is covered in one transaction with the run transition.

It also arrived unverified — the fixer said plainly it couldn't run Postgres in its sandbox. So I applied the same standard to it that caught my own bug. Dropped and recreated the dev database so the migration file itself ran, confirmed the trigger existed, then drove the stamp through `markWatcherRunCompleted()` — the real production writer, not hand-written SQL. It fires.

The verification chain, all on a booted server:
- Three real Behavior runs dispatched, all failed at the model, column stayed `NULL` — the negative case came free.
- Real completion writer → stamp lands on the run's own `completed_at`, same transaction.
- Listing endpoint returns them ordered by the stamp; archiving one drops it immediately while its stamp stays.
- Mutation check: making the trigger's `WHEN` unable to match takes the scope-all suite from 18 pass to 3 failed. My first attempt at that mutation was wrong — I renamed the trigger, which doesn't disable it — so the initial "still passes" reading was my error, not a real result.

Final diff is 4 files. The two transcript files net back to `origin/main` exactly, which is correct: the trigger design touches neither.

Updated artifact with the new recording and both dead designs: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22

**Confidence: high** on the write path, the listing read, and the archive behaviour — each exercised against a live DB with a mutation check behind the tests. **Medium** on production fidelity of the completion step: no LLM finished a run here, so I invoked the settle function directly rather than having a worker reach it naturally. **Low** on backfill cost — the prod `runs` row count is still unmeasured and dbmate wraps the migration in a transaction.

Next:
1. Size `runs` on prod before merge — that backfill is the one unbounded thing left.
2. Merge once CI and `pi-review` are green, then prod-verify that archived Behaviors actually drop from `personal-agent`.
3. Rebase the owletto Recent sidebar branch onto this — it's the only consumer of `scope=all` and the only way to see these rows in a UI.

perf(server): move the Behavior stamp backfill off the watchers lock

The migration was transactional, so ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN held ACCESS
EXCLUSIVE on public.watchers until commit -- across the one-time runs history
aggregation at the bottom of the file. Run it transaction:false so each
statement commits standalone: the column add is a momentary catalog-only lock,
the partial index builds CONCURRENTLY (with the repo's inlined INVALID-carcass
heal), and the runs scan takes nothing stronger than ROW EXCLUSIVE.

Co-authored-by: Codesmith <codesmith-bot@users.noreply.github.com>


 ...260730210000_watchers_last_run_completed_at.sql | 53 +++++++++++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 47 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
=== DIFF ===
+-- of this file into the same transaction would run that history-sized scan
+-- *under* ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and stall every Behavior read and write for its
+-- duration. Under transaction:false each statement commits standalone (the
+-- runners split these sections statement-at-a-time; prod: scripts/migrate-up.mjs,
+-- embedded/tests: packages/server/src/db/migration-loader.ts), so the column add
+-- is a momentary catalog-only lock (nullable, no default — no table rewrite),
+-- the index builds CONCURRENTLY, and the `runs` scan holds nothing stronger than
+-- ROW EXCLUSIVE on the rows it stamps.
+--
+-- RETRY SAFETY. transaction:false can leave earlier statements committed with
+-- this migration's ledger row unwritten, so every statement below is written to
+-- re-run: the section converges on replay from any crash point.
 ALTER TABLE public.watchers
   ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_run_completed_at timestamptz;
 
@@ -51,8 +67,28 @@ CREATE TRIGGER stamp_watcher_last_run_completed_at
 
 -- Serves the listing read exactly: equality on (organization_id, agent_id),
 -- ordered by the timestamp, with the two filters folded into the predicate.
--- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation -- watchers is a bounded configuration table; dbmate wraps this migration in a transaction, where CONCURRENTLY is not permitted
-CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS watchers_agent_recent
+--
+-- The INVALID-carcass heal is inlined so it re-runs on every retry: a crashed
+-- CONCURRENTLY build leaves a same-named INVALID index that `IF NOT EXISTS`
+-- would silently no-op over, recording this migration as applied with a
+-- non-enforcing carcass in place.
+DO $heal$
+BEGIN
+  IF EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1
+    FROM pg_index i
+    JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
+    JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
+    WHERE n.nspname = 'public'
+      AND c.relname = 'watchers_agent_recent'
+      AND NOT i.indisvalid
+  ) THEN
+    EXECUTE 'DROP INDEX public.watchers_agent_recent';
+  END IF;
+END
+$heal$;
+
+CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS watchers_agent_recent
   ON public.watchers (organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
   WHERE status = 'active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL;
 
@@ -64,6 +100,12 @@ CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS watchers_agent_recent
 -- use `idx_runs_watcher_id (watcher_id) WHERE watcher_id IS NOT NULL`, where
 -- parsing conversation ids out of transcript history would force the same
 -- unindexable scan this change exists to delete.
+--
+-- Runs in its own transaction (see LOCK SAFETY above), so however long this scan
+-- takes it never holds a lock on `watchers` beyond ROW EXCLUSIVE plus the rows it
+-- stamps. It is placed after the trigger so a completion landing mid-scan is
+-- stamped rather than lost, and the GREATEST/`<` guard makes a replay a no-op
+-- once a later stamp is already in place.
 UPDATE public.watchers w
 SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(
       COALESCE(w.last_run_completed_at, mx.last_at),
@@ -84,13 +126,12 @@ WHERE w.id = mx.watcher_id
     OR w.last_run_completed_at < mx.last_at
   );
 
--- migrate:down
+-- migrate:down transaction:false
 
 DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS stamp_watcher_last_run_completed_at ON public.runs;
 DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.stamp_watcher_last_run_completed_at();
 
--- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-deletion -- dbmate wraps this migration in a transaction, where CONCURRENTLY is not permitted
-DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.watchers_agent_recent;
+DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.watchers_agent_recent;
 
 -- squawk-ignore ban-drop-column -- rollback path for the column introduced by this migration
 ALTER TABLE public.watchers

`owletto-default_watcher_1_run_109` checkpoints under `runId=112`.

review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard (which the earlier note here
told me to KEEP) compares those two spaces, so it can never be true —
`stampBehaviorLastRun` was dead code and Behaviors would have vanished from the
listing entirely. Fix: drop the comparison. `isRunOwnedByJwtScope` already binds
the conversation id to the authenticated run, and the UPDATE re-fences org+agent,
so the behaviorId parsed out of the verified conversation id is trustworthy.

The unit test agreed with the bug: its fixture built the conversation id from the
same runId it minted the token with, so the two spaces coincided — a shape
production never produces. See [[feedback_test_the_shape_production_throws]].
Fixture now inserts both rows. Mutation-tested (broken guard → 1 fail).

Live red→green on `:9186`, same request both times:
RED `200 {"id":1}` + `last_run_completed_at` NULL;
GREEN `200 {"id":1}` + `2026-07-30 20:08:41.374+01`.
Then: `GET /lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/history/threads?scope=all` returns the three
Behaviors ordered by the stamp, and archiving one drops it from the listing while
its stamp stays — the prod bug, fixed. Recorded: artifact
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22

**No LLM run completed locally — every provider key is exhausted** (Anthropic no
credit, Z.ai weekly limit, Gemini 429, OpenRouter 402, OpenAI 400 on
`reasoning_effort` + function tools for gpt-5.6-sol). Five real Behavior runs
dispatched, all five failed at the model — which incidentally proved the negative
case (failed checkpoints never stamp). The checkpoint POST was driven directly
with a minted worker token; that IS the code under test.

**No UI on this branch consumes `scope=all`** — the Recent sidebar lives on the
unmerged owletto `feat/restore-recent-list`. Nothing to film here.

## The bug

`agent-thread-list.ts` derived Behavior rows at read time: leading-wildcard
`LIKE '%\_watcher\_%\_run\_%'` + per-row `regexp_match` + `GROUP BY` over
`agent_transcript_snapshot`, once per agent per sidebar render. Unindexable,
grows with run history forever.

Worse, it was unfixably stale: archiving a Behavior does not unmake its past
runs, so the derive path had nothing to filter on. **22 of personal-agent's 26
Behavior rows in prod were archived Behaviors it could never drop** (prod:
4 active / 56 archived org-wide).

## REJECTED approach (already built — do not resurrect)

Gave Behaviors a `conversations` row keyed `behavior:<id>`, kind `'behavior'`,
plus a trigger on `watchers` to sync name/status/agent_id. It worked and passed
every gate, but needed: a CHECK-constraint widening, a DB trigger, a
`FOR UPDATE` race guard, three `kind <> 'behavior'` leak guards in
`findConversationById`/`getConversation`/admin scope, and a fix for a
listing-row-strands-on-agent-reassignment bug **that the design itself created**.
Half the mechanism defended against problems the design introduced — the
coordination-brake smell. Behaviors are not conversations.

## ACCEPTED approach

One column on the bounded config table, then union at read time.

- `ALTER TABLE watchers ADD COLUMN last_run_completed_at timestamptz`
- partial index `(organization_id, agent_id, last_run_completed_at DESC)
  WHERE status='active' AND last_run_completed_at IS NOT NULL`
  (squawk needs a `-- squawk-ignore require-concurrent-index-creation`; watchers
  is ~60 rows in prod)
- **backfill reads `runs`, NOT `agent_transcript_snapshot`** — no regexp, no
  LIKE, groups on a real FK:
  `SELECT watcher_id, max(completed_at) FROM runs WHERE run_type='behavior' AND
  status='completed' AND watcher_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY watcher_id`
- write: `transcript-routes.ts`, same completed-checkpoint site, single-row
  `UPDATE watchers SET last_run_completed_at = GREATEST(...)`. **Keep
  review-fix's `intent.runId !== args.runId` guard.**
- read: bounded select on watchers; `status`/`name` read LIVE so archive and
  rename need NO sync at all — that is where all the deleted machinery goes.
- `conversations-store.ts` reverts fully to `origin/main`.

**Do NOT check `last_fired_at` or `updated_at` as the timestamp** — measured on
prod: `last_fired_at` is NULL on every Behavior that ran today (it is
event-cooldown bookkeeping) and `updated_at` tracks scheduler/definition writes,
disagreeing with the listing on 3 of 4 active Behaviors.

The AGENTS.md invariant, the deletion of the derive block, and the red→green
test `drops an archived Behavior even though its completed runs remain` (its
assertion holds under either design; proved red against
`git show origin/main:...agent-thread-list.ts`). Delete the
agent-reassignment test — that bug cannot exist when the row IS the watcher.

## Gotchas hit

- `behaviors` is NOT a view: `table-schema.ts:422` is an explicit column
  allow-list mapping to physical `watchers` (`['behaviors','watchers']` at :745).
  A new column is NOT auto-exposed to `query_sql` — opt in deliberately.
- **The vitest/bun harness re-runs migrations on startup**, so mutating a
  trigger via `psql` is silently reverted before the test runs and yields a
  meaningless pass. Mutate the migration FILE instead. See
  [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].
- Changing an already-applied migration needs the test DB recreated
  (`dropdb/createdb lobu_test` + `CREATE EXTENSION vector, cube, earthdistance`).
- squawk lints the **down** path too — `constraint-missing-not-valid` fired on a
  plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` there. CI pins `squawk-cli@2.58.0
  --exclude=ban-drop-column,require-timeout-settings`; `bunx squawk@latest` is a
  DIFFERENT, unrelated package.
- Test fixture traps: `watchers.created_by` is FK-constrained to `"user"`, and
  `idx_runs_executing_per_behavior` allows only one in-flight run per Behavior,
  so a helper that checkpoints twice must settle each run first.

## Unverified

Prod row counts for `runs` / `agent_transcript_snapshot` — neither is in the MCP
query allowlist. dbmate wraps migrations in a transaction, so **size them before
shipping the backfill**.

lines: -**STATUS 2026-07-30: committed `bf0cc78c6`, then BOOTED — and the boot caught a

+fires `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF status, completed_at, watcher_id, run_type,

Both hit on 2026-07-30 while shipping #2370. `pi-review` is a REQUIRED check, so
a broken reviewer blocks merge outright.

## Codex quota

`make review` (default `REVIEWER_CLI=auto` → codex outside a codex harness) died
with `ERROR: You've hit your usage limit … try again at Aug 5th, 2026`. The gate
**fails closed on purpose** and will not silently fall back to another reviewer.

Switch explicitly: `REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable make review`.
`review_validate_claude_model` accepts only `fable`, `opus`, or `claude-opus-*`
(`scripts/lib/review-reviewer.sh`) — matching [[feedback_use_fable_for_review]].

## The claude reviewer's $schema rejection

```
Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: no schema with key or ref
"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
```

`scripts/review.sh` passes `prompts/review-output-schema.json` verbatim via
`--json-schema`, and the Claude CLI's validator does not resolve that meta-schema
ref. Nothing to do with the diff under review.

Workaround — **working tree only, never commit it** (it belongs in its own PR,
not whatever branch you're shipping):

```bash
cp prompts/review-output-schema.json /tmp/review-schema.bak
python3 -c "import json;p='prompts/review-output-schema.json';d=json.load(open(p));d.pop('\$schema',None);json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)"
REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable make review
cp /tmp/review-schema.bak prompts/review-output-schema.json   # restore IMMEDIATELY
```

Dropping `$schema` removes only the meta-schema declaration; the constraint body
is unchanged, so the verdict is still schema-validated. Verify with `git status`
after restoring — a stray edit here would land in the next commit.

## Re-running review is sometimes mandatory, not a loop

`make review` posts `pi-review` against a specific SHA. If anything moves the
head — including the Codesmith bot pushing to your open PR branch — the new head
has no status and the PR sits `BLOCKED` with nothing explaining why. review.sh
detects this and refuses rather than attaching a verdict to a stale commit. That
re-run is not the find-fix loop [[feedback_review_is_last_gate_not_the_loop]]
warns about.

**Merged: PR #2370, squash `48ce06156`.** Five files, all nine required checks green.

The ending was messier than the middle, so here's what actually happened after my last message.

**A Codesmith bot pushed to my open PR branch twice, mid-flight.** First an identical `QUERYABLE_SCHEMA` entry to the one I'd just committed (I dropped mine rather than fight it), then a genuine improvement I hadn't made: the migration was transactional, so `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `watchers` across the history-sized `runs` backfill scan — stalling every Behavior read and write for its duration. It moved that to `transaction:false` with a `CONCURRENTLY` index and an inlined INVALID-carcass heal. That closes the one risk I'd flagged as open.

Both arrived unverified — the bot can't run Postgres — so both got the same treatment as my own bug: dropped the dev database, re-applied the migration from scratch, confirmed the trigger exists and the index came out `indisvalid = t`, and re-drove the stamp through `markWatcherRunCompleted()` on the final head. Clean.

**CI caught something I'd recorded and then walked past.** The schema-drift gate failed because `behaviors` is an explicit column allow-list over `watchers`, not a view — a new column is never auto-exposed. I had that exact gotcha in memory from the earlier session and didn't act on it. That's the one avoidable round-trip in this whole sequence.

**The review gate needed two workarounds.** Codex is out of quota until Aug 5, and the Claude reviewer path rejects the repo's own `review-output-schema.json` over its `draft/2020-12` `$schema` ref. I ran Fable against a working-tree-only copy with that key stripped, then restored it immediately — the real fix belongs in its own PR, not this branch. Fable returned **bug_free 90, 0 bugs, 0 blockers, risk low**, and notably ran the migration through the embedded migrator itself, which is independent confirmation of my verification rather than a restatement of it.

Artifact (recording + both dead designs): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f78dc2b1-5d85-4adf-8ae8-77fb1b265f22 — note it documents the checkpoint-route design, which is now history; the shipped mechanism is the trigger.

I've scheduled a wakeup to poll the rollout and then confirm live that the 22 stuck archived rows are gone. Next after that:

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
   If it doesn't need another iteration, stop instead (step 6) — re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then make the same decision. If the loop should continue, call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 (the Monitor remains the wake signal; the new wakeup is only the fallback heartbeat). If the event means the work is finished, stop (step 6).
6. **To stop the loop** — the task is complete, further iterations can't make progress, or the user asked you to stop — call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` (no other fields) and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context).
